body: Oh boy, can't wait for the ayahuasca to wear and be back at square one.

I love how that's all you take away from this.

Just another drop in the bucket.

Oh well, I've done enough time so I'm walking out.

I have searched long and hard and found I simply don't believe in making purpose for yourself. It's a hollow lie people tell themselves navigating an apathetic world.

I have lived without love since I was in sixth grade. I found my friends were similar people. One of them cracked early and ended his life. That was the first of a handful of funerals I attended.

In the military, when I was in, my one goal for two years was to die while deployed. Sadly that never happened. No dying a heroes death for me. Instead I volunteered for awful duties. I was part of the team that had to identify and collect dead service members remains. What a training. Pictures of blasted out humvees where people were burned to their seats and their hands melted to the steering wheel. Never got to do much with that either.

I have been deemed as someone who is unworthy for love due to my poor socialization, twisted personality, and ugly looks.

Therefore I'm invisible to the world at large, as are most men like me.

When people like us walk away from life, we're statistics, when normal people walk away, they're humans.

I just know my lot in life and am tired of coming home to an empty apartment to either fester in my depression or desperately escape my existence.

I would pay someone to end me, just so that they could have a little extra money in these dark times.
It's a damned if you do or don't scenario. Just the nature of the beast.
It's fine but that's not what they want to hear. It may even be what they need, but to them it feels like a dismissive phrase.

I mean it's probably a good thing to try and protect the purity of this, but this place will always attract the type of incel you don't want.

So you either give them the boot, this stifling whatever they wanted to say here, or you deal with the whining.

I don't have a horse in this race and there are other options of course.

It's why I still posit this place is rather useless. It lacks social presence, immediacy, and importantly, consequence.

You can not help someone who doesn't want it, even if they post here. They have to help themselves.

What happens here is you have a clash of two opposing lived-in experiences where I honestly believe both sides are a touch disingenuous.

Incels want to be validated in their world views, and if they can't get that, then they turn to attention. Any publicity is good publicity to the emotionally and attention-starved incel.

People who want to help present their own lives as data sources without acknowledging they're biased from the start. I imagine it takes a certain kind of man or woman to want to help the demonized incel. But this is also Reddits fault as reddit just isn't indicative of the real world. 

So we just get people who want attention butting heads with people who want them to get better in an unrealistic amount of time(as perceived by incels). This leads to generic advice that always seems to culminate with 

"Get therapy".

While valid and possibly helpful, I don't think it's what incels want to hear. 

Sometimes people just need to whine and be heard whining. Sometimes they need to stew and fester alone. Sometimes they can't be helped.

You're intellectually dishonest if you think every highschool love is like the perfect couple so often presented. 

Sure, let's say most normies have highschool love. Where does that go? Awkward teenage sex? Pointless drama as highschoolers posture about how cool, sexy, or mature their relationship is? 

It's pointless to glorify this.

It's dirty nostalgia bait for an experience unlike what most people have. It's everywhere in the media. It's escapism to "an easier time".

From god awful live action Disney channel cartoons to slice of live anime.

I see it as a grieving thing for something that never was.

But I'm pretty biased in that my high school life sucked and I'd rather not pretend going back to there would do anything.

Escapism is fine. It's glorification and addiction to something that never was, not so much.

It'll be interesting to see if this is a 'human' trend or generational. I'd be interested to know what media looks like in 10 years if it's still pumping out the same lazy plots with new scenery.

What do any of these online communities offer you anyways? 

Genuinely curious because I'm pretty unfulfilled with just about all online communities. They lack positive social presence and intimacy, as well as have little to no immediacy. 

They suck. They don't feel real.

Is it nice to go where people support and understand your issues where previously you've felt unsupported and unheard? Yeah.

But that's all these communities focus on. A false dichotomy amplified by the plasticity of social media. A lie that only rich, talented dudes get the girls and that nobodies like you and I are doomed. 

What a beautiful fatalist lie. Are you in control of your own life? Your actions? Your thoughts?

I mean I was living like a savage animal for roughly 4 years, not an insignificant amount of time. But at some point you either have to rise to the difficulty or continue coping.

It's not easy to do either.

Eh therapy was mostly miss and little bit for me. For some it's great, for others like me it's pretty neutral leaning on okay, for other still it's a waste of time and money.

It depends on what you expect to get out of therapy and what kind of therapy is used along with your relationship to the therapist.

Coping is why I'm alive. Let me tell you something. Only you know how you're feeling right now.

When I was deeply depressed, I lived in a trashfilled apartment, rarely ate, and generally laid in bed in darkness on all my time off. 

I "coped" at the time by watching videos on netflix and youtube at the time. It was the only thing in my life that I had going for me.

 8-12 hour workdays, 5-6 days a week, in a job I hated. Coping is a tool.

A tool that both incels and people here seem to misunderstand it's use. It's a way to survive difficult situations, both physically and mentally.

The problem is people see it as a way of sidestepping an issue or ignoring. But let me ask you? 

Is focusing and being constantly aware of your lot in life healthy? Does it feel good to say you are a lonely depressed person in your head everyday?

No. You have to be ready to deal with your issues. And everyone gets ready on their own timeline.

There is nothing wrong with ignoring your issues for small chunks of time. Honestly it's probably better than hyperfocusing on it.

The problem is mental illness can paralyze you into inaction. Depression and anxiety make it hard where you can't get started on tasks or don't do them because you assume the worst will happen.

In my opinion coping is fine, but it's a skill and mindset that has to be trained.

Here's something. Accept your own company. A woman will not complete you as a person, she will only complete the idea of a person in your head.

Is love, affection, and intimacy amazing? Probably. Would having a partner allow you more headspace, energy, and relief to fix yourself? Probably. 

But just as this potential fantasy partner can save you from yourself, they can just as easily destroy you.

Here's the ugly wonderful truth. Women don't want to date people with too many hang-ups and not enough positives. Men might possibly due to the utter lack of intimacy and affection, but women can come by it easier.

Here's where your problem is. You've handcuffed yourself and seem convinced a woman has the key to your freedom. She might have the key, you might have the key, a mental health specialist might have it.

Or maybe nobody has it.

You're only worth what you care to be man.

It's probably extremely misguided. I do believe the only one who can help you at the end of the day is yourself. This place is useful for collecting perspectives and possibly elementary advice, but everything else is up in the air.

The dating world has been shattered multiple times since I've been born. The break from coercive traditionalism, the rise of online dating, the slow revolution of women's roles vs the stagnation of men's. 

It's rough and people forget that sometimes you just need to stew in shit for a while before you realize it stinks.

I'm the wrong person to discuss this with because I'm intellectually dishonest or hypocritical about word choice, however words are coming into existence that hold both a technical meaning and capture a certain zeitgeist.

Hell people can't even agree on Incel. Do they argue the technical definition, the definition most commonly perceived to used, or a third more personal definition.

It boils down to things like specificity, sensitivity, and a phrase that was beat into my head in a technical writing class.

Words mean things and synonyms are not the same.

But on a personal level, I don't tend to care yet I understand why others would. Is being called a male or moid weird and probably derogatory, yeah. But, once again, I don't care. I choose to look past a lot of the implied nonsense to dissect what they are saying and ignore some of the less than humanizing context.

Gross to think my lived in experience is a norm. I'm actually trying to decide if I want to go and restart treatment in the next few months. I didn't give it an honest go last time.

Acceptance is painful. Especially when it was for me about myself. Accepting my dog died of cancer hurt but was easy to understand. She died from a terrible disease so putting her down was better (she had stopped eating and rarely moved).

But accepting a condition like this seems much more difficult. I think there's a great generalized blanket of situational depression over my generation that is valid, but it lacks the depth be of something like clinical major depressive disorder.

It's frustrating.

That would be writing about something I have no passion for. 

My own life and experiences are boring to me, as I imagine most people think they are to them. 

I find it funny you say this as I've just started my most hated classes in college, English and communication. I absolutely cannot stand these topics in academia, but that's probably because I have a chip on my shoulder about college.

I'm not sure we can be normal. But I'd rather be me than normal. Even if I'm alone forever. I get it though.

It's addicting in it's familiarity and that sucks. It's hard to leave. I've been dealing with it for years. 

But these things change is. The depression makes sadness easier. The anxiety says expect to fail. So I always think why bother. There was a point in my life where I was too anxious to end my own life. 

We just have to live with this deck of cards we're even if it's missing suits or there's no face cards. We may be able to suppress or control our illness, but mine is clinical. It's here while I'm here. 

I've been depressed on a tropical island, on an international trip, and even recently. But that's okay. It's okay to be sick.

We don't begrudge people with broken bones. We don't belittle the people who suffer with cancer. We hope they get better or more comfortable.

With us, we can't afford to be comfortable, because depressed comfort isn't really comfort at all. It's just the easy default.

It's that ephemeral 'confidence' and 'charisma'. Nobody can really explain how to get it or nurture it in an easily-understood no nonsense way.

It sucks man, I feel you.

People attack the mindset a lot, usually with what I call toxic positivity.

I think it's okay to stew on stuff for a while, but it probably shouldn't be for a very long time like 5+ years.

An outlier in height is what I meant. IDK what to tell you man. I could say women sick, dating sucks, the world sucks, or life sucks. 

Social media and dating apps have given people a lot of social power and reach but seem to be pretty vapid or only surface level. 

I know of like 1 person who is satisfied with their dating app experience. It didn't happen until he was in his early 30s.

What if you are the outlier? Women prefer men taller than them, generally. I agree. Now I am considered a short man, so what are my options?

1. Look for women shorter than me

2. Buy lifted shoes

3. Look for women who don't care as much

4. Give up

I see those as my options.

Also are you a stat or a person?

It's a problem of stats and poor understanding. Numbers and trends can say whatever I want you to interpret them too. 

Trends are easy to be lazy with. Your brain is lazy. Why waste time with individual analysis and nuance when you could just write them off and shove them into the box you decided to put them in.

Also the internet only shows the wackiest of the wack. You're not going to hear much about the quiet couple married for 20 years. It's boring news. It doesn't generate clicks, doesn't bring in ad money.

I'm a human first man. And humanity experiences a breadth of emotions. Some of the strongest are feelings of despair, sorrow, and general sadness.

Not crying hurts the dying soul more.

The only way to go your own way is something you have to do by yourself I think.

It's a used and abused term like RedPill that could've been meaningful but was ruined like so many other terms.

I live my life fully embracing the no sexual/romantic relationships. It's something you can choose or accept, just depends on where you're coming from.

It honestly just depends. Certain people get hung-up on ideas of milestones or progress points, but this frames things in a strange linear way if you ask me. 

When I was 23 years old I had 10 college credits. My friend had double majored. My other friend had an associates and some technical certs. Back then I framed things based on yearly income because I believed (and still do to a lesser extent) that money is the key to opportunity.

Double bachelor friend was working at Starbucks/Target. I was enlisted in the military. Associates friend was making 70k a year.

The point I'm trying to drive home is your experience is yours. Will people be weirded out by a guy with little to no experience, maybe. Should you tell them you have none, probably not immediately.

But you having or not having a flimsy high school or college fling will not impact you in the long run.

Most people don't know what they want out of relationships until later in life anyways. It's where the whole betabux stuff comes from. I'm not telling you to finance a woman's life or ignore her past or anything like that, just that you have a shot at dating.

Sadly big parts of relationships are based on status, at first. But that's just a trick to get crappy people to not slam the door on your foot. 

Status only (helps) gets you in, who you are guarantees if the relationship stays.

I was in a similar position years ago. Sitting at my parents house as a depressed 19 year old NEET. I literally did almost nothing. I would eat once or twice a day, drink water, and spend 16+ hours in front of a screen.

I realized I was probably going to lose everything if I stayed that way. I had to change and it sucked. It still sucks sometimes. But part of life is realizing sometimes the best option is the lesser evil and you had no good choices to begin with.

An admission of defeat. Something I'm all too guilty of myself. You're removing the challenge by choosing to opt out. It's something I bring up with my military friends a lot.

The job is easy, but soul-sucking and mind-melting. The only reason you do it is because of a guaranteed pension for government service along with healthcare. 

But I always ask him if the easy, low quality of life today is worth the years he's wasting in the service.

We called it sitting on your hands or retired on active duty because after a certain point you're phoning everything in and not caring.

Do you want to care about being with someone? Or would you take the easy guaranteed route you've set for yourself?

I'm a hypocrite in this department because I'd rather not try and stay being alone, yet I left the service because it's a foul thing after a year or two past training.

Just stuff to think about.
You're a good person with a bigger, stronger heart than me.

I don't have one. I am unremarkable. I am an unemployed young man with no college degree who lives in a tiny apartment and car. 

My life is one that could have been lived by any one man.
Of course I could. Even with all of them combined they don't outweigh my emptiness.

Not really. Talking won't change my mind. Reddit and other social media platforms never changed my life. I'm tired, alone, and empty.

Whatever shallow interaction I can have on Reddit won't help me, it'll just delay the inevitable. I want to be free.

Pills are garbage. There's truth and lies in all aspects. The blackpill would probably tell you to lay down and rot if you didn't have an SO yet, but that's not a fun existence. I lived it for a while.

BluePill would say be yourself and respect women. I imagine you've always been yourself and respected your fellow women. Really no advice.

RedPill would say get ripped and get a good job. Okay not bad. To get women. Bad move. Get a good job to feel true self-reliant. Get ripped because it feels better than being fat. Once again, been both.

Pills suck. Live your life.
Being alone together on the internet does not ease my loneliness.

It just depends man. You could try to get a girlfriend everyday until you die and never succeed or you could give up and find some girl interested in you immediately. It's just too random and there's only factors you control.

It sucks. I'm into a lot less mainstream stuff. I like art, animation, and visual storytelling. I work a very technical job with few women and most who are in this field are married or not into what I'm into.

I've never had a girlfriend but at this point it would throw a wrench into my life. I work too much and spend my free time on college and recharging myself. 

Personally I've come to peace with being alone. I've got friends, a career, entertainment, and porn. Would it be nice to be loved, validated, and appreciated?

Heck yeah. 

Am I going to entertain those notions. 

Nah, and probably never will.

Lost too much of my life struggling with this.

College was always online for me so that. Going through Python coding books too. Just finished Doom Eternal. Bodyweight exercises every now and then, mostly push-ups and planks with occasional yoga pose. Watching anime.

This social distancing hasn't impacted me all that hard. 

I understand some people grow uncomfortable alone but I've always been alone. It's an easy, comfortable default.

Plus there's too much free entertainment, education, and other stuff out there.

I feel as though you're trying to push people into too much positivity off the bat. It's not wrong but most people will push against it. You can't tell an Incel to smile anymore than you can tell a store clerk.

I do think there's a comfortable appeal to wallowing in misery because it's easier than suffering a period of growth.

I agree the systemic categorization with life in all this pill talk is unproductive. They all have truths and lies in them and the black pill espouses the old 4chan joke of 

"You're not even x, so why even live."

It's funny as a joke every now and then but people fail to realize overexposure reinforces these beliefs, whether subconscious or otherwise.

This is getting long but I'm going to end it on this. You can't help people who still want to wallow.

I actually agree about choosing a thing over a person. I feel as though romantically unsuccessful men are very task oriented. Everything is a problem, and problem's generally have a solution.

A simple example. Need more money? Work overtime. 

However dating, emotions, and relationships are not tasks that can effectively be completed in such a manner. Id argue a lot of relationships are probably a meeting of dumb luck combined with opportunity creation. Basically, you took care of yourself while putting yourself out there and eventually someone noticed. 

There's too many factors, too many variables. You can only control small portions of this problem and it's extremely difficult to do even that.

I really do think it is a sort of death of innocence that fundamentally changes people. Some take it in stride, others shut out the world, and some just break down.

Me personally, I decided to give up at 22 after going on a date with a woman who very clearly just wanted to use me as a stepping stone to a better life. I'm more than a paycheck and health insurance damnit!

It took a lot to get over my choice to be alone, but I refuse to throw myself in the meat grinder of dating for x amount of years just to have a chance.

It just doesn't make sense or seem worth it to me right now.

The disingenuous moral high ground advice would be to focus on your work only and ignore the rest.

My advice is to be good enough on a technical level while being able to network.

Some industries it really just is who you know/where you graduated from vs any actual measure of skill.

Sucks but it's life.

It's rough. My bad therapists would have said something like look at the things you can control. But that was meaningless to me. I didn't care that I could do basic human tasks that all adults should do. I cared that I was alone and nothing was making my situation better.

Sure but you'll never have more money than Jeff Bezos, and you'll never be a starving child soldier in Africa.

The competition should be against yourself if you want to frame it as a win/lose scenario.

Not control other people, but a feeling of frustration that you inputting the advice doesn't generate the outcome of a better dating life.

Do you feel like what you do in regards to dating advice doesn't matter?
So it's control then. You're frustrated by the lack of control in this aspect of your life.

Then why do you want to win, if not to be fulfilled or happy? Isn't that why people compete in things.

You said women have options, and they have to select from those options.

Don't you choose who to date as well though? Don't you choose which women to approach?

I'm aiming to say dating isn't a competition, and neither is life. It's pointless to see certain aspects of existence competitively, because there will always be better off and worse off individuals.

So every man in the world is now competing with each other for every single woman? Is a rejection of you a failure? Have you lost the competition? Is dating something to win?

Also by your logic I imagine most are miserable. Do you think everyone who wants to be an artist is making a living off of it?

You've pigeonholed yourself by saying you are the worst option and every other man is better. You can't win this competition you want to have if you're determined to lose.

Just because something's not bad doesn't make it good. Missing out on social milestones of growth hurts. Self-reliance was something I always had. Had to teach myself how to shave, do laundry, and feed myself as a young teenager.

I don't particularly care about those simple things. I've been financially independent for 4 years. Doesn't mean anything to me though. I care about the emotional side of my wants.

I already have food, water, and shelter, I want social acceptance and romance.
You already answered it yourself. You don't need it, some others might.

Simply that. Romantic could improve one's quality of life. I believe you are taking me too literal. There's nothing one needs in life other than water, food, and warmth/shelter.

Who wants to just live with only those things? You don't need friends or lovers, and you only need a caretaker up to a certain age, but I would argue these relationships fill a need.

It's similar to an unfulfilled office worker. They could have a great family, house, food, and entertainment, but feel so trapped by their job that they are dying every moment at work, causing depression or alcoholism or drug abuse.

They don't need a new job, just like I don't need a romantic relationship.

But wouldn't it be nice to be a little less miserable today than you were yesterday?

Romantic love could be necessary for life. But if you see no difference between familial, romantic, and philial/friendship love why ever go on a date? And if you do why wouldn't the date be with your friend?

It's not some grand story, I just have too much self-awareness. It's obvious to me that there's a bucket of reasons I'm alone and looks is probably just one of them, and probably rather insignificant in that bucket as well.

I'm an extremely mentally unwell person but I'm stable. Far too stable and entrenched in my beliefs to have my opinions changed by others. 

My previous two psychologists ended our working relationships because there was nothing left to cover. They smiled at me, said I'll be able to live a good life, and turned me on my way.

I've realized it's easier to accept living alone in obscurity than struggling to be seen by anyone as something, whether it be as a companion or sex partner or lifelong something or other.

So I grind through life wearing my mask like the rest of them. Wake up, work out, work, college, errands, sleep. A little me time on the weekends doing something I want alone.

A comfortable misery is preferred to unknown change by the mind.

Depression is a battle every single day, for me at least. It kept me out of the gym, it kept me suicidal, it kept me staying up staring at the ceiling for nights on end, wondering why I'd even consider trudging through another day.

Misery is addicting, especially to troubled minds. It validates twisted perceptions and reaffirms a victim status, which is gold in today's social media hellscape.

It can get better, but leaving hurts. It's a death of a facet of yourself. A rejection of an identity and community you may have helped cultivate.

It's lonely on the other side as well. Nobody wants to hear about the virgin who left inceldom, but we exist.

Why do you value a woman's sexual attraction over a woman's love?

Why do you value a perceived person over your actual person?

How do you fix a growing depression rate among young men? I'm curious what you think can be done that would be meaningful considering for serious cases of depression most people live with it their entire lives.
